chapter: Early drum sets and dance-hall era
title: Fish fries, suppers and bar licenses
summary: Fish fries were replaced by suppers, which bar owners opposed, and permits and licenses became costly.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Did you ever go to many fish fries?
Oh, after I got big enough, yeah, I went around a lot of them.
Who do you think broke up fish fries, why they don't have any?

Well, that supper came in, they stopped calling them fish fries, they started having suppers. And they had suppers where they used to use a jug box in them, and guys was... He was making a real party or a dance out of it, you see. Instead, this is supper, like they used to have time back with the red lanterns. Yeah, start to make what you call a real dance out of it. Then they went into, I think some kind of law went into effect that they had to do it. They had to get permits and to sell beer because, you know, suppers began to sell beer, whiskey, and everything else in it. Well, I think that the bar Ramon is the one that complained about it, if I'm not mistaken. And they called for permits, when the permit was so high, so they just kind of cut that out for a while. Mm-hmm.

Ain't everything. They're moving that too. Yeah. I remember a time when you had a fish fry. You might get a permit, it would probably cost you around about 75 cents. The policeman would pass by, and he'll pick it up and go on to bed his business. That was all to it. And after the suppers, they start giving these suppers and selling these tickets. And like I said, they begin selling wine and whiskey and suppers. And they're making a real dance out of it. And it might start, the supper might start around by 7 o'clock that night, maybe 7, 8 o'clock the next morning. They're still having supper, supposed to be supper all as solid as the bed and wine and dancing and having a lot of fun. And I think the bar Ramon owners, they're the one that proprietors begin to take about it because it was taking a lot of the bar Ram's business.
And the bar Ram, like if anything else, they paid a big license to operate the bar.
Yeah, that cost some money to buy a license, right? Yeah.
So I imagine that was kind of slowed up on the suppers. From the fish ride to the suppers, and on the suppers they ain't dying out too.
But when you had the blue lamp, did your license cost you much? That's quite expensive.
Yeah, well during that time I think it's around 700 and something for the license. And they have gone up about $300 to $400 more now I think. And here in the quarter you can't get them.
